svg.title: Separate population alleles from an individual genotype
svg.desc: The Iᴬi×Iᴮi square combines Iᴬ or i from one parent with Iᴮ or i from the other, each gamete at one-half. Offspring IᴬIᴮ, Iᴬi, Iᴮi and ii each have one-quarter probability and score AB,A,B,O respectively. AB means both A and B antigens are detectable, not a blended antigen. Three named alleles occur in the population while a typical diploid individual carries two at this locus. Multiple alleles describes population diversity; codominance describes products within a genotype. The simplified classroom inheritance model is not sufficient for a medical decision or unique identity inference.

g.text: Separate population alleles from an individual genotype
A specified simplified ABO cross demonstrates codominance and multiple alleles.
Parents: Iᴬi × Iᴮi. Each parental gamete has probability ½.
Three named alleles in the population; two at this autosomal locus in one diploid individual.
AB displays both antigens, not a new blended antigen. Codominance differs from multiple alleles.
This simplified classroom model cannot establish unique identity or make a medical decision.
